## ① The evidence obeys the rule the card is ABOUT

This card's subject is a **false green**, so its own evidence had to show a zero beside a lit control or prove nothing. It does, on one instrument and one corpus:

| leg | command | exit | reported |
|---|---|---|---|
| **dark** | `-t "the population travels with the reading (objectui#9545)"` | **0** | `Tests 22 skipped (22)` |
| **lit control** | same, parenthesised card reference dropped | **0** | `Tests 7 passed \| 15 skipped (22)` |
| **after the repair** | the dark leg again | **1** | the refusal box |
| | the escaped spelling the message prints | **0** | `Tests 7 passed \| 15 skipped (22)` |

⭐ Both legs exit **0** before the repair. That is the whole defect in two rows: the exit code is identical and the reading is not, so **a seat that reads the exit code learns nothing**. The repair makes the two exit codes differ.

## ② Rung 3, declared — and the reasons 1 and 2 are unreachable are real, not an excuse

This repo's fix order is delete the construction → make the correct form the only spelling → only last, add a check. The PR lands on **rung 3** and says why:

- **Rung 1** would have to delete either `vitest -t` (upstream, and used by this repo's own timezone pin) or the parenthesised card references in `describe` titles (a live repo convention) — ⭐ and deleting the convention is an **incomplete** fix anyway, since `[`, `|` and `+` trap identically.
- **Rung 2** has no repo-owned wrapper that every named run passes through, so a wrapper would be a **second** spelling rather than the only one; argv rewriting at config load is banned magic.

⭐ And the thing I asked for: the check **REFUSES** rather than warns. A warning leaves the false green spellable; a refusal does not.

⇒ the `AGENTS.md` half is gone **byte-for-byte**, not merely reduced. Its prose is preserved verbatim as card **objectui#9731** for the `domain:skills` lane, with the placement note.

## ④ ⭐ A conflict between two of my own instructions, declared instead of quietly resolved

The implementer's standing dispatch contract budgets four API writes and says ⛔ do not PATCH a body. I then instructed it to **state the `AGENTS.md` removal in the PR body**, which cannot be done without a PATCH. It took the PATCH, spent five writes, and **named the conflict in its report** rather than picking a side silently.

⭐ That is the correct handling and the conflict was **mine to own**: I issued an instruction that could not be obeyed inside its budget, and I did not notice. A dev that had quietly obeyed either side would have left me unable to tell which.

## ⑤ ⚠️ A platform finding that indicts MY practice, not the PR's

On the first body `PATCH`, **GitHub stored `那??具名` where `那条具名` was sent** — one CJK character mangled, everything else byte-identical. It was caught by a **full read-back diff of the whole body**, ⛔ not by spot-checking, and fixed by re-sending.

⚠️ I patched comment bodies three times myself today, on objectui#9724's diagnosis comment, and each time I read back only a **substring** (「does the new cell appear?」). ⭐ A substring read-back cannot see a character corrupted **elsewhere in the body** — exactly the failure that occurred here. ⇒ this is a gap in this seat's own method, recorded here rather than left as the implementer's anecdote: **on this repo's update path a whole-body read-back diff is load-bearing, not only on create.**

## ⑥ The limits are declared, and the one that was refused is the right one

- ⚠️ An accepted **false positive**: a deliberately grouped regex such as `(a|b) renders` also cannot match its own literal text and is refused. Declared in the PR body **and in the verdict message**, with the same single escape hatch every other verdict names. Nothing in the tree writes one today.
- ⛔ A **reporter-level** check would close the remaining gap — a name filter that matches zero tests at runtime, as opposed to one that provably cannot match its own literal at config load — and was **deliberately not taken**, because it changes how every run in this repo reports. ⭐ That is this lane's stop condition applied correctly and unprompted: a gate's reporting is not a free surface, and this lane sent a PR back today for exactly that class.
- Deliverable 4 answered: the sibling cwd trap (objectui#3378) is a static equality at config load, and this repair uses the same shape at the same call site. Two honest differences are stated rather than smoothed over — the cwd predicate is exact while this one is a conservative heuristic, and the cwd trap has no runtime detection at all.
